#!/bin/bash
#flux: --constraint=haswell
#flux: --job-name=test_driver
#flux: --time=40:00:00
#flux: --nodes=9
#flux: --mail-user=hrluo@lbl.gov
#flux: --mail-type=ALL
# The Slurm QoS directive '--qos=regular' does not have a direct equivalent in Flux.
# This is a site-specific policy and is usually handled by queue or resource constraints.
# The 'salloc' command from the original script has been removed. 'salloc' is used to
# create a new, interactive allocation, which is redundant and incorrect within a batch
# script that has already been allocated resources.

module load python/3.7-anaconda-2019.10

module unload cray-mpich
module unload cmake
module load cmake/3.14.4

module unload PrgEnv-intel
module load PrgEnv-gnu

export MKLROOT=/opt/intel/compilers_and_libraries_2019.3.199/linux/mkl
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/opt/intel/compilers_and_libraries_2019.3.199/linux/mkl/lib/intel64
BLAS_LIB="${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_gf_lp64.so;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_gnu_thread.so;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.so;-lgomp"
LAPACK_LIB="${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_gf_lp64.so;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_gnu_thread.so;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.so;-lgomp"

# module use /global/common/software/m3169/cori/modulefiles
# module unload openmpi
module load openmpi/4.0.1
export PYTHONPATH=~/.local/cori/3.7-anaconda-2019.10/lib/python3.7/site-packages
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$PWD/autotune/
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$PWD/scikit-optimize/
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$PWD/mpi4py/
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$PWD/GPTune/
export PYTHONWARNINGS=ignore

CCC=mpicc
CCCPP=mpicxx
FTN=mpif90

cd ~/GPTune/examples/minimalcGP/
pip install -r requirements.txt --user

#flux run --oversubscribe --mca pmix_server_max_wait 3600 --mca pmix_base_exchange_timeout 3600 --mca orte_abort_timeout 3600 --mca plm_rsh_no_tree_spawn true -n 1 python cGP_constrained.py 123 30 1.0 0 4 3 10 SI2.bin


export PATH="/global/homes/h/hrluo/.local/cori/3.7-anaconda-2019.10/bin:$PATH" 

echo 'cGP superLU experiment environment setup finished...'

# Note: The following command is a single serial script. Although 9 nodes are allocated,
# this command will only run on the first node. If 'run_matrix.sh' does not contain
# its own 'flux run' command, the other 8 nodes will remain idle, wasting resources.
sh run_matrix.sh Na5.bin


echo 'cGP superLU experiment done!'

issues: Significant Resource Waste: The job requests 9 nodes but only executes a single serial command (`sh run_matrix.sh Na5.bin`). This command will run on only one of the allocated nodes, leaving the other 8 nodes (and all their cores) completely idle for the entire 40-hour duration. This is an extremely inefficient use of resources unless the `run_matrix.sh` script internally contains `flux run` commands to launch parallel tasks across the allocated nodes.

The script loads an external OpenMPI library (`module load openmpi/4.0.1`). Using external MPI libraries with `flux run` can lead to runtime conflicts, as Flux has its own integrated MPI support. It is generally recommended to build and run applications against the MPI library provided by or integrated with the Flux environment for better stability and performance.
